grammar.label: translating what has no equivalent
grammar.form: compensation, explicitation, borrowing, and the honest footnote
grammar.meaning: carries a meaning across when no matching form exists

explanation.en: Uzbek marks evidentiality with a suffix and English has no such form, so the translator must add a word, lose the nuance, or footnote it. Every translation is a series of these decisions, and the mark of a good one is not that nothing is lost but that the translator knew what was being lost each time.
explanation.uz: O'zbek tilida -ekan qo'shimchasi ma'lumot manbasini belgilaydi; ingliz tilida bunday shakl yo'q. Yaxshi tarjimaning belgisi — hech narsa yo'qolmasligi emas, tarjimon nima yo'qotayotganini bilishi.

grammar.positive_example: There is no English form for the suffix, so the translator added 'apparently' and noted the loss.
grammar.negative_example: There is no English form for the suffix, so the translator ignored it.

grammar.label: false friends and the borrowed word that drifted
grammar.form: actual, eventual, sympathetic, magazine, fabric, intelligent
grammar.meaning: a word that looks familiar from another language and means something else

explanation.en: Russian 'aktualny' is not 'actual' — it means topical. 'Eventualny' is not 'eventual'; 'simpatichny' is not 'sympathetic' but likeable. These are not rare traps: they are the commonest single source of error in advanced Russian-speaking learners, and they survive to C2 precisely because they never look like mistakes.
explanation.uz: Ruscha 'актуальный' — 'actual' emas, 'dolzarb' degani; 'симпатичный' — 'sympathetic' emas, 'yoqimli'. Bular kamdan-kam uchraydigan tuzoq emas — rus tilli o'quvchilarda eng keng tarqalgan xato manbai, va C2 gacha yashab qoladi, chunki ular xatoga o'xshamaydi.

grammar.positive_example: The question is topical, not 'actual'; nothing in English carries that sense.
grammar.negative_example: The question is actual and therefore of interest to the committee.

l1_notes.uz: Rus tilidan kelgan soxta do'stlar C2 darajagacha yashab qoladi, chunki ular xatoga o'xshamaydi.

body.text: How do I put Navruz into English?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: You do not. Call it the new year and half of it is gone; leave it as Navruz and the reader has nothing at all.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: You write the name, and then you show what it means by what people do. Two lines of a scene will carry it. One word never will.

body.speaker: Dilnoza
body.text: The ministry wrote 'actual figures' and meant the current ones.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: A borrowed word that drifted. It kept one meaning in one language and took another here, and both sides believe they are reading the same word.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Enough that I keep a list. 'Sympathetic' is the one that catches everybody.

body.speaker: Dilnoza
body.text: Because for us it means good-looking.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: And in English it means kind about your trouble. A reference letter can go badly wrong on that one word.
